name: Load Lightening
summary: At the Mirage Raceway, Pozzik’s goblin crew seeks lighter parts for its racers. Hollow vulture bones may strengthen the steering and frame without adding heavy metal.

sections.title: Every Ounce Counts
sections.body: Across the Shimmering Flats, goblin and gnome engineers race to win by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust matters little if a car carries too much weight. Gnome teams favor intricate gears and brass fittings. Pozzik’s goblins strip away dense iron framing and replace it with lighter hollow parts wherever they can.

sections.title: Desert Scavenging for Speed
sections.body: Pozzik looks to the salt wastes around Thousand Needles instead of importing costly composites. Salt Flats vultures are plentiful, and their bones are hollow, honeycombed, strong under strain, and light. His mechanics work them into the racers’ steering rigs and smaller braces. They hope the machines can outmaneuver the gnomes without shaking apart at top speed.

faq.q: Why does Pozzik want vulture bones for a race car?
faq.answer: Goblin engineers use vulture bones because they are hollow and light. Worked into delicate parts such as the steering rig, they add strength without weighing down the racer.
Pozzik leads the goblin racing crew at the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats. He directs the goblin pits against their gnome rivals.
Vultures circle the open Shimmering Flats, especially near the huge skeletal remains scattered across the northeastern salt basin.
The Mirage Raceway is a neutral racing ground on Thousand Needles’ dry salt lake. Goblins and gnomes race dangerous experimental rocket-cars there.

faq.q: Are the gnomes doing the same thing?
faq.answer: The gnomes also seek lighter racers, but their tradition favors precision clockwork and complex metals. Goblin mechanics rely more on salvage and improvised parts.

faq.q: Does this work help with Pozzik's larger racing effort?
faq.answer: Yes. Lightening the racer earns Pozzik’s trust and leads to more work amid the rivalries and goblin sponsorship on the flats.

angles.text: Pozzik’s use of bird bones shows goblin ingenuity: practical, improvised, and effective at reducing a racer’s weight.
A classically trained Tinker Town engineer might be scandalized to see goblins lash scavenged bird carcasses into steering rigs.
